title: Universal factorization before Stein connectedness
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a universally closed and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $B=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and factor $f$ as $X\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{s}\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization]. Then $q$ is universally closed, quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and surjective; $s$ is integral; $q_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$; and this factorization is the relative spectrum of $f_*\mathcal O_X$ and commutes with flat base change.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY, label lemma-stein-universally-closed, line 15087), clauses (1)--(5) and proof

proof.text: Use Scheme.toSpecΓ_steinFactorizationBase to identify the composite with f. The second map is a Spec map and hence affine and separated. UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated gives universal closedness of q. QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f and quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f give compactness and quasi-separatedness of X; the standard toSpecΓ instances give quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of q.

Mathlib Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean:256 gives IsDominant X.toSpecΓ for compact X (its appTop is the canonical ΓSpec isomorphism). Universally closed q has closed range, so surjective_of_isDominant_of_isClosed_range (Morphisms/UnderlyingMap.lean:252) gives surjectivity. Apply UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective to q followed by s to obtain universal closedness of s. The equivalence IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom makes s integral.

On each basic open D(a) of Spec Γ(X), the qcqs localization computation is Mathlib isIso_ΓSpec_adjunction_unit_app_basicOpen (Morphisms/QuasiSeparated.lean:450-465). Equivalently this is degree-zero flat base change along the affine localization Spec Γ(X)[1/a] -> Spec Γ(X), with the canonical global-section isomorphism. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.isIso_iff_isIso_basis to conclude that the canonical sheaf map is invertible. Forgetting gives IsIso q.c, and pushing forward gives the required canonical algebra identification along s.

For the two Cartesian squares, flatness of b is MorphismProperty.of_isPullback applied to the flipped first square and Flat g. For each affine open W of B-prime, apply isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right to the second square with U_S=top, U_X=top, U_T=W, U_Y=q-prime inverse W. This is the affine-open version of degree-zero flat base change. The map q.appLE top top is q.appTop, hence ΓSpecIso.hom and invertible. Therefore pushout.inr is invertible. Its composite with pushoutSection is q-prime.app W by pushout.inr_desc and appLE_eq_app. The canonical sharp map is consequently invertible on the affine basis. Apply isIso_iff_isIso_basis and then functorial preservation of isomorphisms by pushforward along s-prime.

lean.statement: theorem stein_universally_closed_factor {A : CommRingCat.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec A) [UniversallyClosed f] [QuasiSeparated f] : UniversallyClosed X.toSpecΓ ∧ QuasiCompact X.toSpecΓ ∧ QuasiSeparated X.toSpecΓ ∧ Surjective X.toSpecΓ ∧ IsIntegralHom f.steinFactorizationBase ∧ IsIso X.toSpecΓ.c ∧ IsIso ((TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} f.steinFactorizationBase.base).map (⟨X.toSpecΓ.c⟩ : Scheme.sheaf (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) ⟶ (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} X.toSpecΓ.base).obj (Scheme.sheaf X))) ∧ (∀ (T B' X' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Spec A) (_ : Flat g) (b : B' ⟶ Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) (s' : B' ⟶ T) (x : X' ⟶ X) (q' : X' ⟶ B'), IsPullback b s' f.steinFactorizationBase g → IsPullback x q' X.toSpecΓ b → IsIso ((TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} s'.base).map (⟨q'.c⟩ : Scheme.sheaf B' ⟶ (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} q'.base).obj (Scheme.sheaf X'))))
lean.note: Relative Spec is rendered by its canonical algebra identification along the integral (hence affine) second map; flat base change uses arbitrary Cartesian squares, not only affine bases.
